text: Seven o'clock. Sirens wail across Busan's harbour. Out at sea the water glows violet, and Kanghan's barge is listing.
In his office, Branch Chief Yang ignores the phone ringing from Seoul and hits the emergency button himself. Seoul can fire him tomorrow. Tonight, he evacuates.
Every phone in the market lights up at once. Leave the waterfront. Move uphill.
In Geum's tent, Seoa grabs the market's megaphone. The aunties are emptying the market, and they follow her.
She stands on a fish crate and runs the evacuation like she ran Mangwon's. Don't run, and don't stop.
On the market roof, Bomi streams the evacuation routes to almost three million people.
Then Choi's van screeches in. Seoa said dinner at seven, so he brought a healer.
Yerin jumps out with her first-aid bag. Jaeha sends her to Seoa, to keep the crowd moving.
Seoa pushes her brother toward the breakwater. She's got the market. She did Mangwon. Go.
So they walk out to the neck of the breakwater, the same spot where Geum held the line ten years ago.
Three seconds left.
The lid bursts. Stone slabs the size of buses fly into the sky, and the sealed gate is open again.
And out of the water come the brine crawlers. Hundreds of them.
Gate mana floods the harbour like snow. In a break, field form comes back after a minute.
Jaeha puts two fingers to his temple. Nib, Borro, Lyra, Pim. Summons go first.
All four flare into field form at once: amber, green, blue and lilac.
Pim hears the whole swarm at once. Most of them are coming up the left side, out of an old storm drain.
Nib tears through the first wave.
Lyra pins them to the rocks, one arrow after another.
Borro shoves an entire wave back into the sea.
And at the neck of the breakwater, exactly where she stood ten years ago, Geum swings her ladle once, and the whole wave turns to ash. The Wall of Busan is back.
On the pier, the old fishermen take off their caps.
Ten years she's waited for this, and she tells them so.
But on the left the crawlers are climbing the market's sea wall. There are too many. They'll reach the crowd first.
Then a truck skids up, and twenty-eight white husks leap off it in perfect unison.
Moon Ahin raises her baton like a conductor. Number four. Where does he want her orchestra?
A wall along the sea wall, Jaeha says. And he'll carry them. With his heart? They're carrying us, so he carries them.
As each husk runs past, Moon Ahin touches its shoulder and gives it a name. Saebyeok. Haebit. Byeol. Noeul. Come back to me.
The husks lock arms along the sea wall, and the swarm breaks against them. Every one of them is linked to Jaeha.
Twenty-eight husks: a load of a hundred and sixty percent. In the Han River pit, twenty-nine was two hundred and forty. The training worked. It's still too much.
His heart starts to stumble.
Geum glances back at him and frowns.
Then the boss of the sea gate comes up. A back too big to see the end of, with rusted plates from the old lid stuck in its hide.
On the barge, the engineers do what Baek ordered. Fire the anchors. Chain it.
Four harpoons slam into her back.
And she keeps coming, towing the whole barge behind her like a toy.
The chains finally drag her to a stop, a hundred and fifty metres off the breakwater, thrashing.
The links are stamped with the same mark as the chains on the farm.
Nib knows those chains. They held his commander.
Operator, those are the same chains. I know, Jaeha says. Go.
Nib runs straight up a chain, thirty metres above the water.
At each anchor, he knocks out the shackle pin with the hilt of his knife.
On the barge, Han Sora takes aim at him with her crossbow, and then lowers it.
The last chains whip free and lash across the barge's deck.
Nib lands back on the rocks. No more chains.
And the Deep Lantern rises to her full height over the harbour. A leviathan a hundred and fifty metres long, with a lantern on her crest burning violet.
Her small, ancient eye finds Jaeha.
Her voice comes out of the sea. Operator? You stopped. Pim goes cold. She thinks he's the man from ten years ago.
Then her lantern pulses, and violet light washes over the harbour.
The crowd stops. Then they turn around and walk back toward the water, their eyes glassy. Choi and Yerin grab whoever they can.
And Seoa lowers the megaphone and walks toward the edge of the pier.
Jaeha is two hundred metres away. He can't reach her. But Pim can.
Pim climbs a harbour light tower, opens his wings, and screams a signal across the whole harbour. Don't listen to her. Listen to me.
Seoa blinks awake with her toes over the water, and Yerin pulls her back.
On Bomi's stream, four million people watch a moth save Busan.
And Seoa picks the megaphone back up. Everyone, back uphill. Don't look at the light.
Then the Deep Lantern raises a hand fifteen metres wide over the breakwater.
Geum steps in beside Borro. Two walls.
The hand comes down, and they hold it: Borro's shield and Geum's ladle, side by side, with the whole crowd behind them.
To keep Borro standing, Jaeha carries him too. Twenty-nine at once. Blood runs from his nose and his ears.
His heart rhythm goes irregular.
The world starts to go grey.
Geum shouts back at him from under the hand. That's how he died. He carried until he couldn't, then he stopped carrying, and they died.
Then what is he supposed to do?
Don't carry it. Hold it.
A wall doesn't push back. It holds.
So Jaeha lets the husks go. Ahin, they're yours. She catches all twenty-eight on her baton.
The husks crack, but they hold, while she whispers their names.
His load drops from two hundred and ten percent to sixty. His heart steadies.
Then he puts both hands on Borro's back. Pass me the next one. All of it.
Store is ready.
And the Deep Lantern lifts her hand higher than before, for the next blow.
